title: How I would build a product aggregator in 2026
decision: Choose and design a UK product-aggregation vertical with explicit commercial search demand, relatively low paid-search CPC, high order values, and enough breadth to support a durable editorial and comparison brand.
methods: Google Ads GenerateKeywordHistoricalMetrics through Leadmap's authenticated read-only runner
Commercial-intent keyword construction using for sale, buy, price, cost, quote, and inherently transactional made-to-measure phrases
Canonical keyword selection by product family to avoid adding identical or close-variant metrics twice
Live-web verification of merchant programmes, retailer pricing, platform documentation, competitor purchase paths, and UK guidance
Current industry reports covering UK affiliate investment and international publisher compensation preferences
Named public practitioner interviews and panels representing publishers, advertisers, agencies, networks, and tracking specialists
Public-company annual reports and current comparison-platform commercial documentation for adjacent revenue-model evidence
Current primary platform documentation for shopping-agent interfaces, merchant feeds, generative-content guidance, and direct merchant distribution
Mechanism-level AI-disruption ledger separating observed platform capability from adoption, economics, and inference
AI scores use a zero-to-five exposure or advantage scale by dimension and are not summed into one recommendation
Volume-weighted CPC calculated as sum(searches multiplied by CPC) divided by sum(searches)
exclusions: Broad informational head terms from commercial-demand totals
Unverified average order values inferred only from visible product prices
limitations: Average monthly searches are rounded trailing historical averages, not obtainable traffic.
Google Ads may group close variants; the scored baskets use one canonical phrase per product family.
Paid competition and CPC describe the advertising auction, not organic SEO difficulty.
For-sale machinery searches can mix new, used, private-sale, dealer, and hire intent.
Affiliate programme acceptance, product-feed access, commission groups, attribution, validation, and PPC permission require direct confirmation before launch.
Public interviews, panels, and podcasts were reviewed, but no original first-party interview was conducted for this project.
Platform announcements establish shopping-agent and merchant-feed capabilities but do not establish UK adoption, conversion, attribution, or publisher compensation.
No first-party agent-referred traffic, assisted-conversion, merchant-feed, generated-content productivity, or correction cohort was available.
Trade-body and platform research has declared industry context and sample limitations and should not be treated as merchant-specific commercial validation.
No live campaign, outreach, purchase, form submission, account mutation, or Supabase query was performed.
